name: frailty and falls overview
title: Falls and frailty decision chart: an older adult's fall is never mechanical; check for an acute illness presenting atypically, then intrinsic and extrinsic causes, then the frailty underneath graded on the Clinical Frailty Scale; each column gives what to look for, what to ask and what to do

root.title: An older adult FELL: never "mechanical" — find EVERY cause
lines: falls are almost always MULTIFACTORIAL: a thorough history (with collateral) + physical exam
the leading cause of injury in older adults: fractures, brain injury, fear of falling, long-term care, death

groups.title: 1 · Is an ACUTE ILLNESS hiding behind it?

head: h
Acute illness, presenting ATYPICALLY
frail older adults may not look textbook
look: A "geriatric syndrome" as the first sign
Don't miss: how it shows in the frail
• myocardial infarction (MI): abdominal pain, nausea, delirium
• rapid atrial fibrillation: anorexia, fatigue, FALLS
• depression: NO sadness, appetite + sleep change
ask: Keep an open mind: find and treat the cause

head: h
Intrinsic
from disease or aging
ask: • function: activities of daily living (ADLs) + instrumental ADLs (IADLs)

head: h
Extrinsic
outside the body
ask: • where: inside or outside, a cluttered home?

head: h
Frailty
LOST reserve to stressors · NOT the same as age, comorbidity or disability
look: • weakness, weight loss, fatigue, poor intake
• risk: stroke, diabetes, chronic lung disease (COPD), cognitive impairment, depression
ask: • 5–6: help outside the home, then with bathing
• 7–8: fully dependent; 8 could not recover from a minor illness
